name: New York
climate: humid continental with cold winters and warm humid summers
notes: Off-leash hours in most NYC parks run from opening until 9am and after 9pm — check the NYC Parks Department page for the specific park before your first visit.

name: Los Angeles
climate: Mediterranean with dry warm summers and mild rainy winters
notes: Canyon trails clear by mid-morning in August — early walks before 8am are standard for pads on hot asphalt.

name: Chicago
climate: humid continental with long cold winters and warm humid summers
notes: Chicago Park District requires a Dog Friendly Area (DFA) permit for off-leash parks — check the Park District site for annual permit steps.

name: Houston
climate: humid subtropical with hot muggy summers
notes: Gulf humidity means dogs cool slowly by panting — good walkers add water stops even on 25-minute routes.

name: Phoenix
climate: hot desert with extreme summer highs
notes: Pavement can hit 70°C in July — most local walkers do pre-6am or post-8pm windows from May through September.

name: Philadelphia
notes: Rowhome blocks mean tiny front yards — most Philly owners rely on daily walks for exercise, not gardens.

name: San Antonio
notes: River Walk itself allows leashed dogs, but the crowds and tight paths make quieter parks a better fit for reactive dogs.

name: San Diego
notes: Off-leash beach hours are city-regulated and change seasonally — check the local Parks & Rec page.

name: Dallas
climate: humid subtropical with very hot summers
notes: Katy Trail is busy after work — for anxious dogs, White Rock's north loop stays quieter.

name: Austin
notes: Zilker gets festival closures several weekends a year — a heads-up saves the walker a wasted trip.

name: Jacksonville
climate: humid subtropical, hot and stormy summers
notes: Afternoon thunderstorms in summer are near-daily — flexible walkers with a rain plan get repeat bookings.

name: Seattle
climate: oceanic with long cool rainy winters and mild dry summers
notes: Magnuson has one of the largest off-leash areas in the country — worth the drive on weekends.

name: Denver
climate: semi-arid with sunny cold winters and warm dry summers
notes: Altitude matters — dogs new to Denver can take 1–2 weeks to acclimate to the thinner air on longer runs.

name: Washington
climate: humid subtropical with hot humid summers
notes: Congressional Cemetery famously operates a members' off-leash program — join, don't just drop in.

name: Boston
climate: humid continental with cold snowy winters
notes: Winter walkers earn their pay here — repeat clients look for someone who won't cancel below 20°F.

name: Nashville
notes: Shelby Bottoms has flat greenway miles — better for older dogs than the Warner hills.

name: Portland
climate: oceanic, wet cool winters and dry warm summers
notes: Forest Park's Wildwood Trail is leash-only its full length — off-leash needs a designated area.

name: Miami
climate: tropical monsoon, hot and humid year-round
notes: Between UV and humidity, most Miami walkers avoid 11am–4pm year-round, not just summer.

name: Atlanta
notes: BeltLine paths are shared with cyclists and scooters — a walker who trains ‘tuck in’ commands earns trust fast.

name: Minneapolis
notes: Deep winter walks need salt-safe paw balm — a good walker brings and applies it themselves.

name: San Francisco
notes: Fort Funston is off-leash and famously windy — bring an anchor toy your dog will actually come back for.

name: Las Vegas
notes: Summer walking is a pre-dawn or post-9pm sport — asphalt stays hot well past sunset in July.

name: San Jose
notes: Coyote sightings on trail edges are common at dawn — walkers here keep dogs leashed and close on the first mile.

name: Charlotte
notes: Greenway networks are extensive — a walker who maps 3–4 loops in one neighborhood keeps dogs mentally engaged.

name: Fort Worth
notes: Fort Woof is one of the state's oldest dedicated dog parks — it gets busy on Saturday mornings.

name: London
notes: Most Royal Parks require dogs on-lead near deer or in flower gardens — signs are posted at every gate.

name: Manchester
notes: Heaton Park is one of the largest municipal parks in Europe — plenty of quiet corners for reactive dogs.

name: Birmingham
notes: Sutton Park has grazing cattle and horses in parts — leads on around livestock is not optional.

name: Glasgow
notes: Pollok has Highland cattle roaming the estate — quiet approach and a strong recall matter.

name: Edinburgh
notes: Holyrood Park is Royal Park land — dogs on lead in some zones, off-lead in others; posted at gates.

name: Bristol
notes: Ashton Court has deer parks fenced off from dog areas — stay on marked dog trails.

name: Liverpool
notes: Otterspool is a flat waterfront walk — good for older dogs, exposed on windy days.

name: Leeds
notes: Roundhay has fenced off-lead zones and open lakeside paths — signs mark which is which.

name: Cardiff
notes: Bute Park runs from the city centre out along the Taff — a full loop is roughly an hour at dog pace.

name: Belfast
notes: Belfast Council enforces on-lead in some parks and open in others — check the council park page before a first visit.

name: Toronto
climate: humid continental, cold winters and warm summers
notes: Toronto's designated off-leash areas are mapped by the city — outside those zones dogs must be on-lead.

name: Vancouver
notes: Stanley Park allows dogs on most trails but on-lead — off-lead beaches are separate designated stretches.

name: Montreal
notes: Winter walking is snow-and-salt territory — walkers who use booties or paw balm win repeat bookings.

name: Calgary
climate: humid continental, cold winters with chinook thaws
notes: Calgary has one of Canada's largest off-leash park networks — but coyote encounters are common at dawn and dusk.

name: Edmonton
notes: At -30°C paw protection isn't optional — booties or thick balm keep short walks safe in January.

name: Ottawa
notes: Bruce Pit is a large NCC-managed off-leash area — busy on weekends, quieter mid-week.

name: Winnipeg
notes: Extreme cold snaps push walkers indoors — check windchill, not just temperature.

name: Halifax
notes: Point Pleasant Park is well-loved but tick season runs long — check dogs after every walk from April to October.

name: Sydney
climate: humid subtropical, warm summers and mild winters
notes: Southern hemisphere summer runs December–February — a good walker asks about paw testing on hot asphalt in January, not July.

name: Melbourne
climate: temperate oceanic, cool winters and warm summers
notes: Melbourne weather can shift 15°C in an afternoon — a walker with a rain layer and water in the bag is standard.

name: Brisbane
notes: Summer storms roll in fast — a walker with a return-early plan avoids caught-in-a-downpour finishes.

name: Perth
notes: UV index runs extreme most of summer — early mornings are the standard walk slot, not evenings.

name: Adelaide
notes: Snake activity picks up September through April — walkers who train a solid ‘leave it’ get repeat bookings.

name: Auckland
notes: Some Auckland regional parks close dog access in kiwi conservation zones — check the Auckland Council page before a new park.

name: Wellington
notes: Wellington wind can gust past 100 km/h — a good walker will reschedule on southerly-gale days rather than push through.

name: Dubai
notes: Dubai Municipality requires dogs on-lead in most public parks, and some parks don't permit dogs at all — the Municipality's park list is worth checking before a first visit.

name: Abu Dhabi
notes: Not every Abu Dhabi park permits dogs — the municipality maintains a dog-friendly list and updates it seasonally.

name: Sharjah
pet_friendly_parks: Al Noor Island (leashed pets, check current policy)
notes: Sharjah rules on dogs in public spaces are stricter than Dubai's — verify with Sharjah Municipality for the current park you plan to visit.

name: Ajman
notes: Coastal breezes make late-evening beach walks bearable in summer — pavement inland stays hot much later.

name: Al Ain
climate: hot desert, drier than the coast
pet_friendly_parks: Al Ain Oasis (leashed dogs, check current policy)
notes: Al Ain's inland dryness means slightly lower humidity than Dubai — but daytime highs are equally punishing.

name: Paris
notes: Many central Parisian parks require dogs on-lead — the Bois de Vincennes has fenced off-lead zones.

name: Berlin
notes: Tempelhofer Feld (former airport) has open runways for long-line recall work — a favourite of local trainers.

name: Madrid
notes: Retiro has designated dog zones — outside them, on-lead is enforced.

name: Barcelona
notes: Barcelona limits dogs off-lead to registered off-lead areas — the city maintains a public map.

name: Rome
notes: Villa Pamphili is the largest park in Rome — plenty of shaded pine paths for mid-morning summer walks.

name: Milan
notes: Summer humidity + urban heat island makes late-evening walks the norm July–August.

name: Amsterdam
notes: Vondelpark has posted off-leash hours (early morning and evening) — outside those hours dogs must be on-lead.

name: Vienna
notes: Vienna has designated Hundezonen (dog zones) inside larger parks — outside them, on-lead is the default.

name: Munich
notes: The Englischer Garten has specific off-lead sections — signs at the entrance mark which parts allow what.

name: Lisbon
notes: Monsanto is huge and hilly — bring water on the longer loops even in shoulder season.

name: Dublin
notes: Phoenix Park has free-roaming deer — dogs must be under close control, and off-lead near deer is a fineable offence.

name: Copenhagen
notes: Danish city parks generally require dogs on-lead unless the area is a marked hundeskov (dog forest).

name: Stockholm
notes: Swedish leash laws are strict March 1 – August 20 in wildlife zones — a walker unfamiliar with kopplingstvång should be briefed.

name: Warsaw
notes: Łazienki Park permits dogs but on-lead only, and not in the historic garden core — signs mark the boundary.

name: Zurich
notes: Zurich's canton-level dog rules (leash zones, seasonal wildlife protection) are stricter than the national baseline — check the canton page.

name: Singapore
climate: tropical rainforest, hot and humid year-round
notes: NParks maintains designated Dogs-Off-Leash Areas — outside them, leashes are mandatory.

name: Hong Kong
notes: Most urban parks in Hong Kong don't permit dogs at all — country parks and specific trails are the main options.

name: Tokyo
notes: Off-lead is generally not permitted outside fenced dog runs — Yoyogi has one of the largest.

name: Seoul
notes: Korean law requires leash and muzzle rules that vary by breed — check the local district office for current rules.

name: Bangkok
notes: Lumpini restricts dogs to specific times and areas — verify current signage before your first visit.

name: Kuala Lumpur
notes: Cultural attitudes toward dogs in public vary widely — a walker sensitive to that context avoids busy market streets.

name: Jakarta
notes: Traffic and heat make short frequent walks the norm — 20-minute loops beat one long midday outing.

name: Manila
notes: Rainy season (June–October) needs a walker with a flexible reschedule window.

name: Taipei
notes: Da'an Forest Park has a fenced dog area — off-lead outside it is not permitted.

name: Mumbai
pet_friendly_parks: Sanjay Gandhi National Park perimeter trails
notes: Street-dog interactions are common — a walker who reads dog-dog body language is far more valuable than one who doesn't.

name: Riyadh
notes: Local norms around dogs in public are shifting but conservative — a walker who chooses quiet times and routes respects that.

name: Doha
notes: Aspire Park has shaded loops that stay usable in the shoulder months — deep summer still needs a dawn schedule.

name: Kuwait City
notes: Summer highs above 45°C — outdoor walking is a dawn/dusk activity from May to September.

name: Tel Aviv
notes: Tel Aviv has one of the highest dog-per-capita rates globally — off-lead beach hours are strictly time-boxed.

name: Istanbul
climate: transitional between Mediterranean and humid subtropical
notes: Free-roaming community dogs are a fixture of city life — a walker who's confident with polite dog-dog greetings is a must here.

name: Mexico City
notes: Altitude (2,240m) affects fitness — dogs new to the city may pant sooner than expected on hills.

name: Buenos Aires
notes: Group walks (paseadores with 6–10 dogs) are a well-established local trade — solo walks are the premium tier.

name: São Paulo
notes: Ibirapuera has designated dog zones — outside them, on-lead is the rule.

name: Santiago
notes: Summer smog days push exercise into morning hours — a walker who checks the Índice de Calidad del Aire is ahead of the game.

name: Bogotá
notes: Altitude (2,640m) matters — new-to-Bogotá dogs need short walks the first week to acclimatise.
